sections.label: PORTRAITS
sections.description: Ladies and Gentlemen - from 2005 to now

sections.label: mirror
sections.description: Mirror is inspired by natural phenomena that irrevocably alter our perception of reality. The series focuses on the critical angle between water and air. This optical effect, combined with a referential trick, creates the illusion of a membrane and a distorting mirror — setting a stage in which the subject interacts. The goal is to invite the viewer into situations that appear surreal but are in fact entirely real. The Mirror series has been exhibited in Montreal, Paris, Brussels, and Fort Lauderdale.

sections.label: presence
sections.description: In Presence,the research explore identity by projecting images of the subjects faces on their own bodies. These photographic anamorphoses fine tuned during the shoot, and not in postproduction, make the spectator question his or her vision. Prior to shooting, I visualize the image he wants to achieve by superimposing the different layers of images doing an art installation that will make up the final result. The goal is to divert the spectator’s gaze, which alternates between the projected face and the canvas-body , between surprises and equivocal evidence. Through playful, ambiguous and dreamlike compositions, and despite the nudity of the models, the series seeks to reveal the strength of the authenticity of the posing subject; an intimate body, incarnated and desexualized.

sections.label: parts of life
sections.description: “Parts of Life” is a photographic series I began in 2006, built from candid moments encountered in different places around the world. Rather than focusing on location alone, the work is driven by the emotional energy, tension, and quiet narratives carried by the people and situations within each frame. The series embraces imbalance, spontaneity, and the fragile intensity of moments that could never be staged, offering an intimate perspective on the human experience. Over time, it has become a visual diary of the stories and emotions I have crossed paths with, inviting viewers to find echoes of their own lives in these fleeting fragments.

sections.label: introspection
sections.description: During my digital art residency at the Swatch Art Peace Hotel in Shanghai, returning to my family home deeply impacted my artistic perspective. Working in my childhood bedroom, I saw my creative endeavors in a new light. The photographs in water reflected my varying states of mind, forming the "Introspection" series. These emotional mindsets ranged from feeling trapped to seeking liberation. Many images were captured in the family bath, rarely used in mu childhood due to my parents' ecological beliefs. Flowers from the family garden symbolized our shared roots, while the orange plastic fence represented emotional barriers to embracing my artist identity in a space defined by my engineering past.

sections.label: lookup
sections.description: Started in 2012, Lookup is a serie where i do use the diffraction effect of the water membrane in order to create both surreal and abstract scenery. Those simple scenes of people standing in front of me end up being deconstructed. It pushes ourselves in an imaginary and dreamy reading of a moment, of a reality. Lookup serie started to be released in the end of 2020.

sections.label: natural digital
sections.description: Natural Digital began during the early COVID period, at a time when the digital world was exploding — in art, in life, in how we related to each other. These photographs, captured underwater using fabric, light, and simple objects, look almost computer-generated. But nothing here is digital. No artificial elements were added; everything was created physically and captured as it happened.

sections.label: wet exploration
sections.description:
The world seen from water

Water is a fundamental element. In wet exploration that started in 2007 the world is photographed from the water in order to make the viewer not only discovering urban or country landscape from a very different angle but also to take conscience that we are surrounded by this amazing yet necessary element. 
 
So Far wet exploration takes you from the alps to nyc via marseille, dominican republic, canada and mexico.

sections.label: parallels
sections.description: The PARALLEL series explores the relationship between the underwater world and the world above it, with a focus on the human element. Using water as a medium, I narrate a story and depict interactions between these two realms, and how they intersect through the presence of a person. I use properties of water such as refraction and reflection to create a sense of otherworldliness and challenge viewer's perception of reality. I capture fleeting moments of beauty and energy within the natural world and the human experience. My goal is to create thought-provoking photographs that question the viewer's understanding of reality and the human connection to nature.

sections.label: inside escape
sections.description: New Yorker versus New York Visitors are not touched by the same aspect of the city. While Tourist get amazed by the dense amount of skycrappers and the density of life in the city, New Yorkers are kept in their thought, stress and objectives. Living in NYC for 3 years, Robin, who was also a stressed worker of the city started to look for visual escape within the usual ‘scrap’ that we face when we are living in the city and not looking ‘UP’ anymore. This result in a serie named Inside escape that allows any kind of newyorker to travel.

sections.label: mural abenakis
sections.description:
Mural project for the Abenaki Museum. I was invited by director William Mazzoleni to collaborate on this project aimed at reconnecting Abenaki culture with its ancestral territory. The Abenaki, also known as the People of the Dawn, have a deep connection to nature. Through a series of images, the mural captures this intimate bond, highlighting the beauty and spirituality of the landscape.

Projet de murale pour le Musée des Abénakis. J’ai été appelé par le réalisateur William Mazzoleni pour collaborer à ce projet ayant pour but de reconnecter la culture abénakise à son territoire. Les Abénakis, aussi appelés le peuple du soleil levant, entretiennent un lien profond avec la nature. À travers une série d’images, la murale capture cette connexion intime, mettant en lumière la beauté et la spiritualité du paysage.
